annotation.title_clean: Who Owns The Robot?: Four Ethical and Socio-technical Questions about Wellbeing Robots in the Real World through Community Engagement
annotation.title_en: Who Owns The Robot?: Four Ethical and Socio-technical Questions about Wellbeing Robots in the Real World through Community Engagement
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Axelsson, M.; Cheong, J.; Nyrup, R.; Gunes, H.
annotation.venue: Proceedings of the Eighth AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society (AIES 2025)
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper reporting three community workshops (n=22) with members of the public, women computer scientists and humanities researchers on ethics of robotic wellbeing coaches. Thematic analysis yields four questions for roboticists: is the robot safe, who is it built for and with, who owns the robot and data, and why a robot.
key_provisions_or_claims: Three community workshops with 22 participants using the Social Robot Co-Design Ethics canvas.
Four questions: safety and how we know, built for and with whom, ownership of robot and data, why a robot.
Under-represented communities should be engaged in anticipatory ethical evaluation of robots.
Transparency about robot capabilities is needed to counter unrealistic expectations from media portrayals.
Questions offered as a framework for roboticists to dialogue with users.
